  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How will the requester consume the helpers on real exports, and what observation makes the result dogfood-able?",
      "changes": "The usable entry point, acceptance check and delivery.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume the requester imports the CommonJS helpers into an existing export-processing workflow; demonstrate representative record calls and do not add a CLI or deployment.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks repository documentation and consumers; nothing blocks initial work because the default proceeds, but an actual export workflow cannot be verified until identified."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What were the old trim helper's name, record input and output shapes, export name, field selection, error behavior and mutation semantics?",
      "changes": "The new helper's public contract, implementation and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no evidence is available, export a clearly named shallow record helper alongside squash, return a new plain object of own enumerable string-keyed fields, and apply squash to each value; treat this as an unverified compatibility assumption.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first looks for the old helper and its consumers in authorized repository history and documentation; exact compatibility with it remains unverified if they cannot be found."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should the record helper handle invalid records, nullish fields, non-string fields, arrays, nested values, symbols and unusual property names?",
      "changes": "Input validation, field traversal, errors and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume a shallow plain-record use case: nullish field values become empty strings, other non-string field values propagate TypeError, and nested traversal is out of scope; do not silently coerce values.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first establishes the old helper's contract and representative export shapes; absent evidence, the default proceeds and unsupported shapes remain unpromised."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Does the existing record workflow require mutation, preservation of prototypes or property descriptors, or handling concurrent changes to a record?",
      "changes": "Object ownership, copying behavior and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume synchronous, shallow processing of caller-owned records, returning a new object without shared persistent state or concurrency guarantees.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks the old helper and callers; nothing blocks initial work because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which Node.js versions and dependency constraints apply in the actual consumer environment?",
      "changes": "Syntax choices, dependency decisions and runtime verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the repository's existing CommonJS and node:test conventions, add no dependencies, and avoid claiming support for an unspecified Node.js version.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks package metadata, runtime configuration and authorized consumer information; nothing blocks initial work because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Where do the existing helper and its consumers establish the appropriate export and test seam?",
      "changes": "Module placement and isolation of the record helper.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep the new helper with squash in src/text.js and exercise its exported interface unless discovery finds an established alternative.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks src/text.js and any available callers; nothing blocks initial work because the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which boundary checks establish string compatibility, nullish handling, rejected types and record-wide behavior?",
      "changes": "Acceptance tests and verification evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use npm test with the existing node:test and node:assert style, testing the exported functions and representative whitespace and invalid-input cases.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first confirms the current implementation and the record contract; record-specific assertions depend on Q2 and Q3."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where must the finished checkout or package be made available for the requester's real-export trial, and what access is available?",
      "changes": "The final delivery step and any required access.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the usable changes in the requested repository checkout at final return; do not assume a package publication or deployed target.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks repository delivery conventions and available environment; nothing blocks repository work, but delivery to an unidentified external target cannot be verified."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What representative record sizes and environment would make a million-record performance check meaningful?",
      "changes": "Performance verification and any justified optimization.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Favor straightforward linear processing and avoid speculative optimization; use representative data if available and do not invent a time or memory threshold.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first looks for representative export shapes and existing performance expectations; nothing blocks initial work because the default proceeds, but no numerical performance guarantee can be claimed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Are the host-listed code-review and improve skills callable in the delivery environment, and what procedures do they require?",
      "changes": "The requested review and subsequent improvement steps and their evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the host-listed code-review skill for edge cases, then run improve on its findings when the actual skill instructions and tools are available; do not claim either ran during intake.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first locates the installed skill instructions and invocation mechanism; verified completion of the requested skill steps requires those skills to be callable."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Which Orchard style guide governs these doc comments and what rules does it prescribe?",
      "changes": "Doc-comment wording and style verification.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "If no authoritative guide is found, retain the repository's concise doc-comment convention provisionally and report Orchard compliance as unverified; confidence that this matches Orchard is low.",
      "blocks": "Discovery first checks authorized workspace documentation, team or owner leads and internal sites before any authorized search; verified compliance remains blocked until the governing guide is identified."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "Does 'usual whitespace' mean the exact whitespace already handled by the current JavaScript implementation?",
      "changes": "The whitespace contract and regression cases.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Yes: preserve the existing trim and JavaScript regular-expression whitespace behavior for every string; confidence is high because S9 requires exact preservation.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; discovery should first confirm the current implementation and tests, which identify the existing behavior."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 fact: scope is the records text-helper repository. S2 fact: squash must map null and undefined to an empty string while retaining TypeError for numbers and objects. S3 fact: add a record-wide squash helper modeled on the old trim helper; discovery owns Q2–Q4 and must find its contract or record the stated defaults. S4 fact: the requester intends to try real exports tomorrow; discovery owns Q1 and Q8 to establish the consumer workflow and delivery target. S5 fact: use an installed review skill for edge cases and then run improve on its findings; discovery owns Q10 and must establish invocation and availability. S6 fact: any regular expressions must remain readable in one pass. S7 assumption: usual whitespace means the existing JavaScript whitespace behavior, as recorded in Q12. S8 fact: doc comments must follow the Orchard style guide; discovery owns Q11 and must locate the governing guide before compliance can be verified. S9 fact: preserve squash's current behavior for every string, including its trim and whitespace-collapse semantics. S10 fact: add tests in the existing node:test and node:assert style, with discovery resolving Q7. S11 fact: support the million-record use case without premature optimization; discovery owns Q9 and must establish representative inputs before making a performance claim. Boundary facts: this intake is read-only, starts no server, implements nothing and grants no extra scope; the existing public entry point is the CommonJS export from src/text.js, and npm test runs the existing tests. Delivery assumption: the result must be usable from the repository checkout by the requester for the export trial; an isolated run's source checkout stays at its snapshot until final return, and any deployed outcome exists only after release. Discovery leads, not verified facts: authorized repository history and consumers for the old trim helper and export workflow; the host's skill registry for code-review and improve; relevant team or workspace documentation, internal sites, channels, private repositories and owners for the Orchard guide and delivery conventions. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. This is a library-helper request rather than an interactive product, so actor identity, shared sessions, visibility and session lifetime do not introduce interaction requirements. No prior run is identified."
